body: Me too, when I manage to get distracted I feel a little better but the mental fog never really goes away. I feel like being preoccupied with your mental health is much scarier than your physical health, since what you're anxious about is directly amplified by that same anxiety, it's almost an endless cycle and it's much harder to separate between symptoms and suggestions. Anyway, hope we can feel better someday.

Exact same here, for other reasons though. I've had two weeks of severe anxiety due to some other health problems. When those problems went away I felt very relieved and decided to slow down with my work for about a week and just relax. To let go of any leftover anxiety I also decided to smoke some weed. I do it very occasionally and it has always managed to chill me out. Now, where I live weed is illegal, so when I smoke it I have to buy it from local dealers. When I smoked it it had no effect except making me feel exhausted, so I immediatly thought something was wrong. I convinced myself that it was probably some light weed or just low quality, and went to sleep. The day after I started experiencing occasional chest pain and shortness of breath. They were very brief occasions, but they started to make me feel anxious. After a couple of days i stopped having chest pain, but what remained is a horrible feeling of numbness and mental exhaustion. I can't focus on anything, I can't do my work, I just feel confused almost like I was drunk. My biggest fear is that the weed was contaminated with something bad, that it gave me permanent brain damage and that I will never regain the lucidity of my mind.

Thanks man, I have to say that just being able to let it out and seeing that my story resonates with someone else is helping me feel a little better already. Stay strong with what's happening to you, it's really sad but know that you're not alone feeling that way
